rows.notes: The paper explicitly states it is a review ('The aim of this review paper is to give some basic benefits, gains and rules of drip irrigation and fertigation'). It reports no data of its own; the statements that drip delivers water directly to the root zone, reduces evaporation and eliminates runoff, and saves 30-50% (or 30-70%) water are taken from cited sources (Postel et al. 2001; Cetin and Bilgel 2002; Chartzoulakis and Bertaki 2015) and Table 1 is reproduced from Shah (2011). Figures are photographs sourced from other works. No own experiment, survey or model run is reported, so Q1 is 'no' and Q2-Q9 are 'no' by rule.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 97-102). The study is a narrative review/overview article, not a primary study; all quantitative claims about drip water saving and reduced evaporation/runoff are secondary.
